focus: A6 commands on both versions: discovery filter, frontmatter semantics, template features, and the v2 replacement for v1 run --command

graphEvents.label: Are command files and semantics dual-compatible?
v1 registers every .md file under the commands tree, like v2
The only discovery filter on v1 is the .md suffix
v2 has no --command; session.command API is the schema-confirmed replacement

label: v1 1.19.3 registers every .md file under the commands tree recursively, exactly as v2 does: all 51 on-disk stems registered with zero omissions, including scripts/README, deep/assets/compiled/*.contract, deep/assets/legacy/*.body and the doctor READMEs. Non-command registration is therefore version-independent and a repo-side convention fixes both hosts at once; it is not a v2 regression.

The only command-discovery filter on v1 is the bare .md suffix: .txt, .md.txt and .md.json under the commands tree were NOT registered, while sub/nofm.md with no frontmatter WAS registered with description null. Frontmatter is optional, so extension layering and relocation are the only reliable exclusion levers.

v1 scans BOTH .opencode/command (singular) and .opencode/commands (plural): probe files foo.md and bar.md in the two directories both registered. The singular/plural split is not a v1 compatibility problem; v2's scannable directory name remains unverified.

No frontmatter opt-out exists on v1: a command carrying command: false and disable: true still registered normally. No frontmatter flag can hide a file on v1, and none is proven on v2, so exclusion must be extension-based or by relocation.

Frontmatter semantics diverge: v1 honors subtask and silently IGNORES subagent; it surfaces agent, model (verbatim incl. #variant) and argument-hint as hints[], and ignores allowed-tools. v2 Config.CommandEncoded declares agent, model (string provider/model#variant or object providerID/model/variant), subagent and subtask as its deprecated alias, and declares neither argument-hint nor allowed-tools. allowed-tools is therefore decorative on both versions.

CONTRADICTION (no halt): v2 2.0.32 GET /api/command returned data:[] for the repo root, for a synthetic tree holding both command/ and commands/ forms, and with --standalone; only builtins init/review appeared when the service cwd was $HOME. This contradicts the earlier orchestrator probe that saw 54 commands including deep/research. Consequence: /api/command must not be used as the v2 registration oracle; use POST /api/session/{id}/command (CommandNotFoundError proves registry lookup) or a behavioural run probe.

v2 run has no --command flag; its only input is message.. . The schema-confirmed non-interactive replacement is POST /api/session/{sessionID}/command with {name, text} required, documenting CommandNotFoundError (404) and CommandExecutionError (500) - the same name-plus-args split as v1 --command plus message. The alternative /name args message form is only PLAUSIBLE: 2.0.32 contains a leading-slash parser returning {name,args} plus a session.command send path, but wiring into run is unproven.

Command-template blast radius is one file each: 40 of 51 commands use $ARGUMENTS, 0 use $1..$N, exactly 1 uses a leading shell injection (!`bash -c ...` in speckit/search.md) and exactly 1 uses an @path include (design/extract.md). $ARGUMENTS appears in both binaries' string tables, so a template port is a one-file decision rather than a 51-file rewrite.

Repo frontmatter census across 51 command files: 45 description, 39 argument-hint, 39 allowed-tools, 7 title, 6 trigger_phrases, 5 importance_tier, 1 version, and ZERO agent, model, subtask or subagent. Every divergent frontmatter semantic is currently inert; the cheapest dual-compat rule is to keep those four keys unused while both hosts must work.

Portable exclusion convention: non-command docs under a commands tree must not end in .md. Renaming README.md to README.txt and *.contract.md to *.contract.md.txt de-registers them on BOTH hosts with no version guard (the repo's existing commands/README.txt and create/README.txt already prove the pattern by never appearing as commands); relocating compiled contracts and legacy bodies under the owning skill's assets/ removes them permanently. Adding a frontmatter flag is ruled out because v1 demonstrably ignores it and v2 is unproven.

direction: A frontmatter flag (command: false, disable: true, or any hidden/disabled key) as the cross-version way to exclude non-command Markdown from command registration
reason: v1 1.19.3 ignored both command: false and disable: true - the file still registered - and v2 Command.Info/Config.CommandEncoded expose no such field

direction: Waiting for or relying on GET /api/command as a shared registration oracle for both hosts
reason: v2 2.0.32 returns only builtin commands (init, review) and data:[] for project directories, while v1 returns 8 fields per command including source, agent, model, subtask and hints; the two response shapes are disjoint
